title: Evaporative Emissions: Where Diagnosis Starts
introduction:
The evaporative emissions system (EVAP) contains fuel vapor and manages its later use by the engine. That is a different job from delivering liquid fuel, so a vapor-system code is not an automatic guilty verdict for the fuel pump.

I use this page as a diagnostic signpost: whether a diagnostic trouble code is present determines which reference to open. The linked diagnostic procedures are required to continue; this page supplies the routing, without the equipment setup, tests or repair decisions.

edits.why: The next reference depends on whether the complaint comes with a diagnostic trouble code.

edits.text: If a PCM DTC—a diagnostic trouble code from the powertrain control module—is present, refer to Electronic Engine Controls (303-14C Electronic Engine Controls - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: A code directs you to the engine-control diagnostic information; it does not, by itself, establish which component needs replacement. The referenced procedure is needed for the actual test sequence.

edits.text: If the vehicle has driveability symptoms without a DTC, refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual. Open Section 3, Symptom Charts, for the symptom-based diagnostic route.
edits.why: The absence of a code does not make a driveability complaint disappear. This branch starts with the observed symptom instead of a code.
